mechanism: Core's AddInputs (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:57-66 at d3056bc) reads the sequence only when sequenceObj.isNum(), widens it to int64_t, and throws JSONRPCError(RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER, "Invalid parameter, sequence number is out of range") when it is < 0 or > CTxIn::SEQUENCE_FINAL before it ever builds the CTxIn. Our createrawtransaction takes the value verbatim -- `for sequence = (or (obj-get inp "sequence") #xffffffff)` at src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:885 -- and hands it straight to (bl.ser:make-tx-in :sequence sequence). The sequence slot is declared (unsigned-byte 32), so SBCL's structure constructor signals a raw SB-KERNEL::TYPE-ERROR. Nothing between there and handle-single-request handles it, so the generic (error (e) ...) arm at src/rpc/server.lisp:416-420 formats the condition into +rpc-internal-error+ (-32603) "Internal error: <the SBCL text>". Nothing checks the type either, so a STRING sequence takes the same path.
consequence:
Malformed input is refused, but with the wrong error class and with SBCL internals in the reply. Executed at the wire, sequence 4294967296 answers {"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: The value
 4294967296
 is not of type
 (UNSIGNED-BYTE 32)
 when setting slot SEQUENCE of structure BITCOIN-LISP.SERIALIZATION:TX-IN"}}; sequence -1 and sequence "foo" give the same shape. Core answers -8 "Invalid parameter, sequence number is out of range" for both integers (rpc_rawtransaction.py:276-280 loops over exactly -1 and 4294967296) and -3 for the string. So rpc_rawtransaction.py:280 fails on the code and the message; a client that treats -32603 as a server fault (retry, failover, alarm) rather than a permanent client error will behave differently; and the message leaks the internal package, structure and slot names. S3 rather than S2: the transaction is never built, no wrong value is returned, and the divergence only appears for input a correct client never sends. The neighbouring checks in the same finding are NOT confirmed as divergences -- a missing vout, a string vout and a negative vout all answer -8 "Invalid input vout" and a negative locktime answers -8 "Invalid locktime", which differ from Core only in wording (Core: "Invalid parameter, missing vout key", "Invalid parameter, vout cannot be negative", "Invalid parameter, locktime out of range").
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3c, warm image. probe4.lisp called bl.rpc::dispatch-rpc-method "createrawtransaction" with inputs built as real hash-tables through %normalize-rpc-params; probe9.lisp repeated them through bl.rpc::handle-single-request + yason:encode. Results: sequence 4294967296 -> LISP TYPE-ERROR "The value 4294967296 is not of type (UNSIGNED-BYTE 32) when setting slot SEQUENCE of structure BITCOIN-LISP.SERIALIZATION:TX-IN", at the wire -32603; sequence -1 -> same, -32603; sequence "foo" -> same TYPE-ERROR on the string; sequence 4294967294 -> OK, tx hex ...feffffff...; {txid} with no vout -> -8 "Invalid input vout"; vout "foo" -> -8 "Invalid input vout"; vout -1 -> -8 "Invalid input vout"; locktime -1 -> -8 "Invalid locktime". Ours: src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:864-897 (the loop, :885 the sequence line), src/serialization defstruct tx-in sequence slot, src/rpc/server.lisp:407-420. Core at d3056bc: rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:41-46 and :57-66. Core functional test: rpc_rawtransaction.py:276-280 (both invalid values, -8) and :282-289 (1000 and 4294967294 must round-trip).
fix_shape: Range-check the sequence in the handler, in Core's order and with Core's text, before any tx-in is constructed. In the createrawtransaction input loop, read the sequence key with %obj-get; when it is absent use Core's default (which is MAX_BIP125_RBF_SEQUENCE unless replaceable is false -- that default is the separate finding fa699133 and should be fixed with it, not silently here); when it is present and not an integer signal the shared %json-type-error with expected type number; when it is an integer outside [0, #xffffffff] signal +rpc-invalid-parameter+ with exactly "Invalid parameter, sequence number is out of range". The same pass should align the neighbouring messages with Core's ParseHashO/AddInputs text ("Invalid parameter, missing vout key", "Invalid parameter, vout cannot be negative", "Invalid parameter, locktime out of range") since they are the same function in Core and the same loop here. Longer term this whole class disappears once a declared-type gate exists (be96017b): the type half of the check belongs there and only the range half stays in the handler. A regression test should assert -8 with the exact sentence for -1 and 4294967296 and a successful round-trip for 1000 and 4294967294, mirroring rpc_rawtransaction.py.
